provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Civic: patriotism
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state what patriotism means.
The pupils should be able to recite the national pledge.
Introduction:
We have learned about good manners and respect for others. Today we will learn about loving our country Nigeria.
Content:
Patriotism means showing love for your country. It means being proud to be Nigerian. We can show patriotism by obeying rules, keeping our environment clean and respecting our national symbols. The national pledge is a promise we make to Nigeria. We say it with our right hand on our heart.
Class activity:
Each pupil will stand up and recite the national pledge in front of the class.
Evaluation questions:
What does patriotism mean?
Name two ways to show patriotism.
Recite the national pledge.
Summary:
Patriotism is love for our country Nigeria and we show it through good actions.

topics.title: Civic: national consciousness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list some Nigerian states and their capitals.
The pupils should be able to identify Nigeria on a map.
Introduction:
We know Nigeria is our country. Today we will learn more about the different parts of Nigeria.
Content:
Nigeria has 36 states. Each state has a capital city. For example, Lagos State has Lagos as its capital. Abuja is the capital of Nigeria and the Federal Capital Territory. We can find Nigeria on a world map. It is in West Africa. We should know our country's location and its states.
Class activity:
Pupils will work in pairs to match state names with their capital cities using flashcards.
Evaluation questions:
What is the capital of Nigeria?
Name one state and its capital.
Show Nigeria on the map.
Summary:
Knowing our states and capitals shows we are conscious of our country Nigeria.

topics.title: Social: division of labour
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify different jobs in the community.
The pupils should be able to explain why all work is important.
Introduction:
In our community, different people do different jobs. Today we will learn why this is important.
Content:
Division of labour means different people do different jobs in the community. For example, teachers teach in school, doctors help us when we are sick, farmers grow food we eat, and mechanics fix vehicles like danfo buses. Every job is important because we all need each other to live well. We should respect all workers whether they sweep the street or teach in class.
Class activity:
Pupils will draw pictures of different community workers and explain what they do.
Evaluation questions:
What is division of labour?
Name two jobs in your community.
Why should we respect all workers?
Summary:
Division of labour helps our community work better when everyone does their part.

topics.title: Social: corruption is bad
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what corruption means.
The pupils should be able to list ways to be honest.
Introduction:
We have learned about good manners. Today we will learn why cheating and stealing are wrong.
Content:
Corruption means being dishonest to get something unfairly. It includes cheating in exams, stealing money or telling lies. Corruption is bad because it hurts everyone. When people are honest, they tell the truth and return what is not theirs. Honesty pays because people trust honest people and they feel good about themselves.
Class activity:
Pupils will role - play situations showing honesty and dishonesty, and discuss the outcomes.
Evaluation questions:
What is corruption?
Give one example of corruption.
Why is honesty important?
Summary:
We should say no to corruption and always be honest in all we do.

topics.title: Security: personal hygiene and health
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list healthy habits.
The pupils should be able to explain why hygiene prevents sickness.
Introduction:
We want to stay healthy and strong. Today we will learn how to take care of our bodies.
Content:
Personal hygiene means keeping your body clean. Healthy habits include bathing every day, brushing your teeth morning and night, washing hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet, and wearing clean clothes. These habits prevent sickness because germs cause diseases. When we are clean, germs cannot make us sick. We should also drink clean water and eat good food.
Class activity:
Pupils will create a personal hygiene checklist to follow at home.
Evaluation questions:
Name three healthy habits.
Why is washing hands important?
What happens if we don't bathe regularly?
Summary:
Good hygiene habits help us stay healthy and prevent sickness.

topics.title: Security: neighbourhood safety
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify suspicious acts.
The pupils should be able to explain what to do when they see danger.
Introduction:
Our compound and street should be safe places. Today we will learn how to stay safe in our neighbourhood.
Content:
Strangers are people we don't know. We should not follow strangers or accept gifts from them. Suspicious acts include someone watching our house, strange noises at night, or people asking too many questions. When we see something suspicious, we should tell our parents, teachers or other trusted adults immediately. We should also know our parents' phone numbers by heart.
Class activity:
Pupils will practice what to say and do when approached by a stranger.
Evaluation questions:
What should you do if a stranger offers you a ride?
Name two suspicious acts to report.
Who should you tell if you see danger?
Summary:
We should always be alert and report suspicious things to adults to stay safe.

topics.title: Civic: democracy for kids
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what voting means.
The pupils should be able to participate in a class election.
Introduction:
In Nigeria, people choose their leaders. Today we will learn how we can choose things in our class too.
Content:
Democracy means people have the right to choose what they want. Voting is how we make choices. When we vote, we secretly choose what we like best. For example, we can vote for our class monitor, best story or best game to play. Everyone should have one vote and we should respect the choice of the majority. This is how we learn to make fair decisions together.
Class activity:
The class will hold an election for the best storybook to read, with pupils casting secret votes.
Evaluation questions:
What is democracy?
Why is voting important?
What should you do if your choice doesn't win?
Summary:
Democracy teaches us to make fair choices by voting and respecting everyone's opinion.

topics.title: Social: national assets
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify national assets.
The pupils should be able to explain why we should care for public property.
Introduction:
Nigeria has many things that belong to everyone. Today we will learn how to take care of them.
Content:
National assets are things that belong to all Nigerians. These include our schools, roads, hospitals, parks, libraries and public buildings. We should care for these assets because they were built with our money. When we damage public property like school desks or write on walls, we are hurting ourselves and others. We should report people who destroy public property and always use public things carefully.
Class activity:
Pupils will walk around the school and identify national assets, then discuss how to care for them.
Evaluation questions:
What are national assets?
Name two national assets in your community.
Why should we not damage public property?
Summary:
We must protect and care for our national assets because they belong to all Nigerians.

topics.title: Security: internet safety
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list safe screen habits.
The pupils should be able to explain what to do when seeing something bad online.
Introduction:
Many of us use phones and computers to learn and play games. Today we will learn how to stay safe online.
Content:
The internet is a good tool but we must use it safely. Safe screen habits include not talking to strangers online, not sharing personal information like our home address or school name, not sending our pictures to people we don't know, and limiting screen time. If we see something scary or bad online, we should tell our parents or teachers immediately. We should also use the internet in places where adults can see us.
Class activity:
Pupils will create posters showing internet safety rules to display in the classroom.
Evaluation questions:
What should you not share online?
What should you do if you see something bad online?
Why is it important to limit screen time?
Summary:
We must be careful when using the internet and always tell adults if we see something that makes us uncomfortable.

topics.title: Revision and project
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to answer questions about values learned this term.
The pupils should be able to create a values portfolio.
Introduction:
We have learned many important values this term. Today we will revise and create a project to show what we know.
Content:
We have learned about patriotism, national consciousness, division of labour, honesty, personal hygiene, neighbourhood safety, democracy, national assets and internet safety. These values help us become good citizens. A values portfolio is a collection of work showing what we have learned. We can include drawings, writings and pictures about the values we studied.
Class activity:
Pupils will create a values portfolio with at least three pages about different values they learned this term.
Evaluation questions:
What is the most important value you learned this term?
How can you show patriotism at school?
Why is division of labour important?
Summary:
We have learned many values that will help us become good Nigerian citizens.
